correctness.rationale: A complete proof obtains exact single- and double-edge nonselection probabilities, diagonalizes the three-class covariance by vertex-edge incidence, proves positive definiteness by the full support of triangle-layer sequences, and expands each eigenvalue with m/n tending to any positive alpha. Exact checker enumeration and exact matrix inversion independently agree with the formulas for small values. At alpha=4/3 only a vanishing leading coefficient is asserted, avoiding an unjustified finite-size sign claim.

originality.rationale: Direct comparisons to the motivating 2019 superposition model, subsequent 2020 adjacent-node bidegree/assortativity results, and 2021 small-subgraph counting limit theorems did not identify an exact inverse-covariance law or the 4/3 asymptotic sign transition for edge-indicator least-squares residuals. A general Johnson-scheme inverse calculation is standard, but does not by itself establish the model-specific transition without the nontrivial covariance asymptotics and spectral cancellations. Relevant mathematical papers and claim records concern other observables and stochastic models; uncertainty about unindexed or stronger prior general results remains.

value.rationale: Overlapping small communities generate random graph edges with positive adjacent marginal association. The full-order linear regression adjustment can reverse its sign, and the exact 4/3 layer-density threshold separates two asymptotic regimes. This characterizes a mathematically natural high-dimensional dependence phenomenon in the established sparse community-overlay model, beyond standard pairwise covariance and degree assortativity.
